question: How do you build an instruction dataset and supervised fine-tune an open-weight LLM (full FT, LoRA, QLoRA) in practice?
contributions: A data pipeline for instruction datasets: filtering, dedup, decontamination, quality evaluation, exploration, generation, augmentation
A synthetic dataset (mlabonne/llmtwin) from crawled articles via backtranslation and rephrasing with GPT-4o-mini
A worked LoRA SFT of Llama 3.1 8B with Unsloth producing TwinLlama-3.1-8B

results.claim: The authors' worked SFT run (LoRA on Llama 3.1 8B, llmtwin + FineTome 10k) took 50 minutes on one A100.
results.setup: Meta-Llama-3.1-8B, LoRA r=32, 3 epochs, effective batch 16, max seq 2048, packing
results.quote: it takes 50 minutes on an A100 GPU

results.claim: Synthetic instruction dataset built from crawled articles yielded 3,335 pairs.
results.setup: GPT-4o-mini, 1,000-2,000 char chunks, Chapter 3 crawled articles
results.note: Text elsewhere says 'five instruction-answer pairs for each extract' but earlier prose says 'three instruction-answer pairs for each chunk'; later calls the dataset '3,000 samples'.
results.where: Creating our own instruction dataset, step 11
results.quote: We obtained 3,335 pairs with this process.

results.claim: Generating the instruction dataset with GPT-4o mini cost under 0.5 dollars.
results.setup: GPT-4o-mini over the crawled raw data

results.claim: A 7B model fully fine-tuned needs about 112 GB of VRAM at 16 bytes/parameter (fp32 weights 4, grads 4, Adam 8); 1,120 GB for 70B.
results.setup: Single GPU, fp32 baseline, ignoring activations
results.quote:
This gives us a baseline of 16 bytes per parameter. This translates into 112
GB of VRAM for a 7 B model and 1,120 GB for a 70 B model.

results.claim: LoRA on all modules with rank 16 gives about 42M trainable parameters for Llama 3 8B, 0.5196% of the model.
results.note: 42M / 8B is about 0.525%; the printed 0.5196% implies a slightly different denominator.
results.quote:
only has 42 million trainable LoRA parameters out of 8
billion parameters, which is 0.5196% of the model

results.claim: LoRA can fine-tune a 7B model on a single GPU with 14-18 GB VRAM.
results.quote: as little as 14-18 GB of VRAM

results.claim: QLoRA cuts 7B fine-tuning memory from 15.6 GB (LoRA) to 9.3 GB, about 40%, and initialisation from 14 GB to 9.1 GB (35%).
results.setup: 7B model; source of the numbers not named in the chapter
results.note: Chapter also says 'up to 75%' peak reduction without a setup.
results.quote: from 15.6 GB for LoRA to 9.3 GB for QLoRA

results.claim: QLoRA trains about 30% slower than LoRA with only minor quality differences.
results.quote: QLoRA being about 30% slower than LoRA

results.claim: Recommended instruction-set sizes: at least 1 million samples for a general-purpose instruct model; 100 to 100,000 for task-specific; as few as 1,000 high-quality for ~70B models (LIMA).
results.setup: Author recommendation based on Yi (<10,000), OpenHermes/Dolphin (~1M), Llama 3 (10M)
results.quote:
we recommend an instruction dataset of at least one million
samples to create a good general-purpose instruct model

results.claim: fineweb-edu-classifier is trained for 20 epochs on 450,000 Llama 3 70B Instruct-annotated samples.
results.quote:
trains it for 20 epochs
on 450,000 samples

results.claim: Hyperparameter used in the worked run: lr 3e-4, linear schedule, 3 epochs, per-device batch 2 x 8 accumulation = effective 16, adamw_8bit, weight decay 0.01, warmup 10 steps, packing.
results.quote:
We train this model for three epochs with a batch size of 2 and 8
gradient accumulation steps (for an effective batch size of 16).

limits: Worked run is not evaluated: the authors say the quick test 'is not to properly evaluate the fine-tuned model'; evaluation is deferred to the next chapter.
Only loss curves are shown; one run, seed 0, no ablations of rank, lr or data mix.
Numbers on QLoRA vs LoRA memory/speed and LoRA parameter counts are uncited in the chapter.
Hyperparameter ranges (lr, batch, epochs) are rules of thumb without sources.
Text has internal slips: 3 vs 5 pairs per chunk, 'Figure 4.11' for 5.11, 'Figure 5.6' cited for inference format.
practices: Start with prompt engineering, few-shot and RAG before fine-tuning; fine-tune only if evaluation misses requirements (When to fine-tune).
Judge instruction data on accuracy, diversity and complexity (General framework).
Use comparative rather than absolute LLM-judge scoring; randomise answer order, normalise length, use a jury of several models; aim for about 80% judge-human agreement (Data quality evaluation).
Add the evaluation set to the dedup stage to decontaminate automatically (Data decontamination).
Fine-tune base models rather than instruct models; if fine-tuning an instruct model, reuse its template (Chat templates).
Use Jinja templates from Transformers; stray whitespace changes tokenization (Chat templates).
Append the EOS token to every sample or the model never stops (Fine-tuning in practice, step 7).
Start LoRA at a moderate rank with alpha = 2 x rank, target all linear layers; raise rank to 64 or 128 if underfit (LoRA; step 5).
Prefer LoRA when memory allows, QLoRA when memory-bound (QLoRA).
Use AdamW (8-bit), weight decay 0.01, warmup about 5% of steps, 2 to 5 epochs, early stopping on validation loss (Training parameters).
Upsample a small custom set with a general dataset (FineTome 10k) so the chat template is learned (step 6).
Monitor training loss, validation loss and gradient norm; use gradient clipping for large norms (Fig 5.11 discussion).

terms.definition: pairs of instructions and answers; instructions are the inputs, answers the expected outputs
providing the expected answer as output and generating its corresponding instruction
LLMs evolve simple instructions into more complex (constraints, deepening, concretizing, more reasoning steps, complicating input) or more diverse ones
re-training a model on raw text; differs from full fine-tuning mainly by dataset structure
combining multiple short samples into one sequence, with attention masks preventing cross-sample attention
erasing knowledge present in the base model when weights are modified
